 Gold Spot / U.S. Dollar Education 14 hours ago XAUUSD Risk & Lot Sizing: How to Survive Gold Volatility
 0 Grab this chart 1 125 Most retail traders blow their accounts on Gold (XAUUSD) not because their directional bias is wrong, but because they use the same fixed lot size on a volatile Gold setup that they use on EURUSD. 
 When XAUUSD expands during the London-New York session overlap (roughly 12:00 to 16:00 UTC in summer time, one hour later in winter), a normal pullback can easily span $3 to $5 in price, and on the 1H timeframe structural swings are far wider. If your lot size is not calibrated to the exact stop-loss distance, a routine stop-out turns into a major account drawdown. 
 Here is the 4-step framework applied to the long setup mapped on the chart (1H). Note: the market is currently closed, so this is a planning example for the next session, not a live trade. Levels must be re-confirmed at the open because of weekend gap risk. 
 - Planned entry: 3,973.02 (buy limit on a pullback) 
 - Stop loss: 3,949.33 (about $23.69, or 237 pips) 
 - Target: 4,020.12 (about $47.10, or 471 pips) 
 - Risk-reward: about 1:2 
 1. Define invalidation first (never the lot size) 
 Before touching the order ticket, mark the structural invalidation point (beyond the recent swing low or Order Block) and measure the distance in pips, using ATR as a volatility buffer. 
 - Wider stop loss = smaller lot size. 
 - Tighter stop loss = larger lot size. 
 - Dollar risk stays 100% constant. 
 2. Understand XAUUSD pip and contract math 
 On most standard MT4/MT5 brokers, 1.00 standard lot of XAUUSD equals 100 ounces. Here 1 pip is a $0.10 move (pip definitions can differ by broker, so check yours): 
 - 1.00 Standard Lot = $10.00 per pip 
 - 0.10 Mini Lot = $1.00 per pip 
 - 0.01 Micro Lot = $0.10 per pip 
 3. Apply the position size formula 
 Lot Size = (Account Balance x Risk %) / (Stop Loss in Pips x Pip Value per Lot) 
 Worked example on a $10,000 account (risking 0.5% = $50): 
 - Scenario A (tighter 120-pip stop, $12.00): $50 / (120 x $10) = about 0.04 lots 
 - Scenario B (this chart's 237-pip stop, $23.69): $50 / (237 x $10) = about 0.02 lots 
 In both scenarios, if the market hits your stop loss, you lose roughly $50 (0.5%). Always round the lot size down, never up. 
 4. Filter setups by break-even win rate 
 Break-Even Win Rate (%) = 100 / (1 + Risk-Reward Ratio) 
 - At 1:1 R:R, you must win 50% of trades to break even before spreads. 
 - At 1:2 R:R (as mapped on the chart), your required win rate drops to 33.3%. 
 Why drawdown math matters 
 Losses and recoveries are asymmetrical. A 10% drawdown requires an 11.1% gain to recover, a 20% drawdown requires a 25% gain, and a 50% drawdown requires a 100% gain. Risking around 0.25% to 0.5% per trade keeps a 6-trade losing streak (about 1.5% to 3%) comfortably inside a 5% daily limit, which matters on funded prop firm accounts. 
 Never hold full-size positions over the weekend: gaps can skip your stop loss entirely, so the loss can exceed the planned risk. 
 Pre-trade checklist: position size, pip value, margin, drawdown recovery and session timing. Run it before every entry, not after. 
 How much % do you risk per trade on Gold, and do you reduce size going into the weekend? Drop your approach below.
